headline: Gulf oil shock and gilt-OAT runs usher in a fractured era of financial repression

events: Spring: French budget collapse after no-confidence vote; OAT-Bund spread blows past 200bp and the ECB activates TPI with conditionality, sparking street protests in Paris
Summer: Iran-Israel exchange escalates into tanker strikes in the Strait of Hormuz; Brent spikes to $135 for six weeks before settling near $105
Record European heatwave and Rhine low water cut industrial output; Indian monsoon failure drives rice export ban
US imposes 'Section 232 plus' tariffs on EU autos and Chinese chips; China retaliates with rare-earth export licensing squeeze
G20 inflation re-accelerates to 5.2%; the Fed pauses cuts, ECB hikes once
UK gilt rout in February after an unfunded energy-bill subsidy; 30-year yields hit 6.4%, BoE restarts QE and the Chancellor resigns
Weak US 10-year auctions and a debt-ceiling standoff push Treasury yields to 5.9%; Fed launches a 'market functioning' purchase facility that markets read as soft yield-curve control
US presidential election fought on inflation and border; razor-thin result contested for weeks, trust collapses further
Pakistan, Egypt and Kenya default or restructure as dollar funding dries up; IMF lending capacity stretched
Chinese coast guard 'quarantine' inspections around Taiwan for 11 days; insurers price a Taiwan-Strait risk premium into semiconductors
G20 inflation peaks at 6.9%
Global recession: world GDP grows just 0.4%; global unemployment peaks at 6.7%
AI capex bust: two hyperscalers cut data-centre spending 35%, Nasdaq falls 38%; firms pivot from building AI to deploying cheap models to cut back-office headcount
Italy requires an ESM precautionary line after BTP spreads exceed 350bp; Germany agrees to a second round of joint EU defence-and-energy bonds
Category 5 hurricane strikes Houston refining complex; US gasoline hits $6.50
Sahel coup belt conflict spills into coastal West Africa (Benin-Togo border war); Serbia-Kosovo armed clashes
Argentina, Ghana (again), Bolivia and Tunisia in sovereign distress
Financial repression era: Japan, UK, US and euro area tighten bank liquidity rules to force domestic sovereign holdings; real rates held negative
Ukraine frozen-conflict armistice along current lines; Russia-NATO incidents in the Baltic continue
Solar-plus-storage boom in India, Pakistan and southern Europe as households and firms flee oil-linked costs; renewables pass 40% of global power
Gen-Z 'cost of living' protests topple governments in Nigeria and Peru; rolling strikes across France and Belgium
US-China 'Geneva accord' caps tariffs at 60% but bans cross-investment in AI and chips; two-standard tech world formalised
Brazil and Indonesia gain manufacturing share as 'connector' economies
Grinding recovery: world growth 2.6%, inflation sticky near 4%
US debt reaches 139% of GDP; Congress passes a VAT-lite 'National Resilience Levy' alongside entitlement age increases, triggering mass AARP-led protests
AI agents used by ~31% of firms; displacement concentrated in clerical, call-centre and junior professional jobs, with wage polarisation sharpening
Record-hot year at ~1.62C; South Asia wet-bulb event kills over 20,000 and accelerates migration to Gulf and Europe
Populist parties lead governments or coalitions in 7 of the G20; climate-and-debt 'Bridgetown 3' swap facility launched with Gulf and Chinese funding

winners: Commodity and energy exporters with fiscal discipline (Norway, Gulf states, Guyana)
Connector economies: India, Vietnam, Mexico, Brazil, Indonesia
Defence, grid, storage and solar manufacturers
Asset-holding older cohorts with inflation-linked or real assets
losers: Indebted frontier economies in Africa and South Asia
Renters and young workers in advanced economies
Europe's energy-intensive industry and southern eurozone bondholders
Junior white-collar workers exposed to AI automation
bullets: Bond markets, not voters, now discipline budgets: France, the UK, Italy and the US all endured yield spikes that forced emergency central-bank backstops and blurred fiscal-monetary lines.
Financial repression is the quiet policy consensus: negative real rates, captive domestic sovereign buyers and capital-flow nudges erode debt slowly while punishing savers.
The 2027 Gulf oil shock and repeated climate disasters made energy security the organising principle of policy, accidentally turbo-charging solar, storage and grid buildouts.
Trade is split into US-led and China-led tech stacks with a tariff-capped truce; fragmentation sits near 73/100 and connector economies arbitrage the gap.
AI diffusion survived a capex bust and is spreading via cheap agents that trim clerical and junior professional jobs, adding to wage polarisation rather than lifting growth much.
Nine sovereign debt crises in five years swamped the IMF; the Global South leans on Gulf and Chinese bilateral finance with strings attached.
Street politics is constant: pension, energy-bill and cost-of-living protests, and populists in power across much of the G20, with institutional trust near historic lows.
Warming of ~1.62C is felt as lethal heat in South Asia and recurring hurricane, flood and drought hits on refineries, crops and insurers.
wildcard: Category 5 hurricane knocked out the Houston-Galveston refining complex for four months in 2029, coinciding with the global recession.
image_description: On a sweltering Lyon evening in 2031, a young delivery rider charges her e-bike from a neighbour's balcony solar panel while a protest march against the pension levy streams past a shuttered bank branch whose window advertises 'Government Resilience Bonds - patriotic savings'.
